subject: [PATCH v9 16/32] mm: zswap: reject high-order swap cache allocations backed by zswap

2026-11-05.patch_summary: This patch rejects high-order swap cache allocations that are backed by zswap when the allocation range overlaps with existing per-page zswap entries. This is because zswap stores swapped-out pages one at a time, and attempting to read back a large contiguous block of swap slots can result in stale or zero data for the slots owned by zswap. The patch adds a check in the __swap_cache_alloc function to reject such allocations and instead falls back to order-0, which is handled per page by zswap_load.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: Approved the patch with a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 11:41 AM Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev> wrote:
>
> zswap stores swapped-out pages one at a time, so a range of swap slots can
> be split between zswap entries and the backing device. A high-order
> swap-cache folio over such a range cannot be read back in one go: the disk
> read would return stale or zero data for every slot zswap owns.
>
> Reject that in __swap_cache_alloc(). Do the check after the folio is in the
> swap cache: from that point zswap can neither start storing nor start
> writing back any slot in the range, so the answer is stable. Callers
> already fall back to order-0, which zswap_load() handles per page.
>
> Co-developed-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
> Signed-off-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

Reviewed-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Approved the patch, but suggested mentioning why rejecting high-order allocations is necessary and proposed a lockless check at the top of the function.

> +	/*
> +	 * Now that the folio is in the swap cache, zswap can no longer start
> +	 * storing or writing back any slot in the range, so this is a stable
> +	 * answer. Reject a high-order allocation over a range that already
> +	 * has per-page zswap entries.

Probably worth mentioning *why* we reject the folio is part of it is in
zswap.

> +	 */
> +	if (order && zswap_is_present(entry, nr_pages)) {

I am curious how often this fails in practice when zswap is enabled and
how often do we end up churning the lock and swap allocation for no
reason. I am mainly wondering if a lockless check at the top of the
function would be useful.

Anyway, this looks good:

2026-11-06.patch_summary: This patch rejects high-order swap cache allocations when zswap is enabled, preventing potential issues with stale or zero data being read from disk.
